author.name: Pauline Kael
author.heading: About Pauline Kael
author.bio: Pauline Kael wrote film criticism for The New Yorker from 1968 to 1991. Her energetic and personal reviews often challenged the division between respectable art and the pleasures viewers actually found in popular movies.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Kael contrasts the pleasures of moviegoing with the values enforced by school and respectable culture. In the passage around this sentence, the cinema’s darkness offers temporary freedom from supervision and moral instruction.
Her argument is about the artistic value of that freedom, not a general instruction to behave irresponsibly. The Joyce attribution loses the film-critical occasion as well as the author.
